# Two people, one metric, four numbers

Sales said revenue was 4.1 million. Finance said 3.8. Product said 4.4. The board deck said 4.2, and nobody could
reconstruct where that one had come from.

None of the four were wrong. Sales counted bookings at signature. Finance counted recognized revenue by period.
Product counted anything with a payment event attached, including the trials that converted and then churned inside
the window. The board deck was an average of three of them, produced by someone who has since left.

The instinct is to pick a winner and force everyone onto it. We tried that in 2024 and it lasted five weeks,
because the sales team's number was not a mistake, it was the number their compensation ran on.

What worked was naming. Four metrics, four names, four owners, four definitions written in one sentence each. Not
one revenue, four things that were never the same thing.

The deck now shows two of them side by side with the definitions in the footnote. The gap between them is a real
signal about trial quality, and for two years it had been invisible because we had been arguing about which single
number to print.

Reconciling to one number would have destroyed information. Naming four preserved it.
